summary: Backend-only validation of the new /api/telegram/internal/pending-users endpoint and the reinforced unauthorized-user webhook logging. 14/14 pytest tests PASSED against the preview backend (REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL). All acceptance criteria from the review request are met: (a) admin GETs 200 with the correct row shape and desc sort by last_attempt_at; (b) anonymous is 403; (c) AGENT (cobranca.teste@pdpv.pt) is 403; (d) authorized-users list/upsert/delete regression still works and seeded user 999000111 is present; (e) webhook rejects bad/missing secret with 403; (f) webhook with correct secret + unknown user returns 200 (Telegram-safe) AND the new synthetic id + first_name appear in /pending-users seconds later; (g) admin login regression OK; (h) Finance /data-health and /dashboard smoke OK (regression from previous module).
critical_code_review_comments: routes.py:120-148 — /pending-users aggregation is correct: match message_type='unauthorized', group by telegram_user_id, $first over pre-sorted stream picks the most recent first_name and last_attempt_at. Good. Minor: the 'first_name' is stored in the 'error' column of telegram_internal_logs which is semantically odd; consider adding a proper 'user_name'/'first_name' field to the log document instead of reusing 'error'. That would also let /pending-users survive if future refactors change what goes into 'error'.

routes.py:41-56 — the secret validation branch is safe: if TELEGRAM_INTERNAL_WEBHOOK_SECRET is unset in production it fails-closed (503). In dev it accepts without header — acceptable for the preview environment.

routes.py:311-332 — _dispatch_update now correctly extracts first_name from message.from OR callback_query.from and passes it to send_unauthorized() AND log_event(error=first_name). first_name is picked up even from a callback (no message), which is good.

menu.py:73-88 — send_unauthorized now shows telegram_user_id + first_name so admin can just get a screenshot. HTML escape is fine because first_name is coming from Telegram (still, if a malicious client sent a first_name with '<script>' the HTML would render — Telegram sanitizes at their end but consider html.escape() defensively).
logs.py:17-43 — log_event is best-effort (try/except) and never crashes the webhook. Good.

SECURITY: TELEGRAM_INTERNAL_WEBHOOK_SECRET currently 'pdpv_internal_webhook_2026' is committed to /app/backend/.env. Rotate before production. Currently OK because webhook was re-pointed to production domain, but the preview also accepts the same secret — a leaked preview secret could be used to spam production logs if reused. Recommend distinct secrets per environment.
test_credentials: admin@pdpv.pt / HCNMEnKMLq (ADMIN, works). cobranca.teste@pdpv.pt / TesteFin2026! (AGENT, works and correctly gets 403 on /pending-users and /authorized-users).
seed_data_creation: Test suite pushed one synthetic unauthorized-user webhook per run with a fresh telegram_user_id in the 800000000-800999999 range and a random first_name (TESTNAME_<hex>). It stays in telegram_internal_logs as message_type='unauthorized' and will surface in future /pending-users calls until logs are trimmed. Also upserts+deactivates a temporary authorized user in the 700000000+ range (TEST_regression_user).
context_for_next_testing_agent: The /pending-users endpoint aggregates from telegram_internal_logs where message_type='unauthorized'. Historical rows for user 1183764773 and 888888888 currently exist and were seen in the response. If those disappear (log purge), test_historical_users_present will skip (not fail) — that is intentional. Webhook secret is 'pdpv_internal_webhook_2026' on preview (env var TELEGRAM_INTERNAL_WEBHOOK_SECRET in /app/backend/.env). Note that Telegram production webhooks now point to tickets.pneusdpedrov.com per the audit — this test suite intentionally targets the preview backend via REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL, which is correct for regression testing.
rca of the issue: N/A – no bugs found. The 3 problems flagged in the audit (webhook pointing at preview, only test user authorized, webhooks spread across 3 domains) are configuration/data issues, not code bugs, and the code-level mitigations (a-d in the request) are all correctly implemented and verified end-to-end via pytest against the live preview backend.
